A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same METok work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-understanding evaluations, computational and memory measurements, component ablations, and frame-scaling experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a 32-frame baseline comparison and MLVU subcategory results.

M1.justification: Event-aware pooling, hierarchical prefilling pruning, and decoding KV-cache removal remain unchanged. Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same procedure and pseudocode.

E1.justification: Both evaluate MVBench, EgoSchema, MLVU, and VideoMME with the same task coverage. The new MLVU breakdown concerns already evaluated subcategories, and v1 already tested 32-frame VILA inputs.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 adds FastV, VisionZip, and DivPrune to the 32-frame VILA scalability comparison, where v1 reported only METok results. The main comparison methods remain unchanged; newly discussed related-work methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds a matched 32-frame VILA comparison across compression methods, including FLOPs alongside accuracy. This extends the baseline evaluation beyond the retained 16-frame main comparison. Existing splits, model configurations, and METok's 16–64-frame sweep remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.3 and Table 8 analyze how performance varies across seven MLVU subcategories. Existing component ablations, hyperparameter studies, frame-scaling results, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added tables do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports METok at 36.5 FLOPs (TB), 52.8 MLVU, and 49.9 VideoMME for 32-frame VILA; its 50.9 MVBench score ties DivPrune. Table 8 adds seven-subcategory scores. Existing table values and figure results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and the mathematical content of Appendix B remain unchanged. No new assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same training-free, three-stage compression claims and 80.6% FLOPs reduction and 93.5% KV-cache savings. The added concluding sentence reiterates the existing emphasis on temporal and semantic preservation.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations about hyperparameter portability, MLVU task-level robustness, and scene, style, and attribute understanding in existing qualitative examples. The limitation to models of at most 13B parameters remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix C newly state explicitly that each base model uses one hyperparameter set across benchmarks without task-specific tuning. Listed parameter values, hardware, and the code-access link are unchanged; this is clarification rather than evidence of changed settings.

R1.justification: Related work adds brief descriptions of AuroraCap, LVC, ST3, VideoChat-Flash, and FastVid, plus other citations including PyramidDrop. The LLaVA-NeXT citation is removed. The central positioning around compression across inference stages remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized terminology edits, including Video to Vision Large Language Models, updates affiliations and acknowledgements, and expands related-work and appendix explanations. It adds subsection D.3 while retaining the main narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 7 and 8, renumbers the former Table 7 as Table 9, relocates Figure 2 and appendix examples, and exchanges the numbering of the pooling and qualitative figures. Conference headers and page layout change, while existing graphical content is retained.

improvement.justification: The added 32-frame baseline comparison supplies controls missing from v1's scalability study, while the MLVU breakdown exposes task-specific strengths and weaknesses. Explicit hyperparameter-sharing information and expanded related work also help assessment. Appendix D.1 overstates the MVBench advantage, which is a tie with DivPrune, but the additional evidence provides a modest net improvement.
